newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slightly easier in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slightly easier in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were slightly easier in early Friday morning trade after opening stronger, but brokers said the undertone was firm due to favourable economic trends in the U.S. and local economies.

"The economic news from the States can best be described as perfect...and put that together with the domestic news here, particularly on the property sector, you have to work very hard to find any reason to be negative,"said Archie Hart, director, equities at BZW Securities Asia.
The Hang Seng Index eased 11 points to 12,993.56, after a 50-point opening jump to around 13,055.
Turnover was active with HK$1.50 billion in shares changing hands after about half an hour of trade.
"We are going to see a relatively firm market in the absence of any negative news," added Hart.

Following the Hang Seng's record-breaking run up on Thursday, when it rose above 13,000 for the first time, brokers did not appear at all fazed by the overnight pullback in the Hang Seng London Reference Index, which dropped 70.15 points to 12,934.65.
"We are bound to have a good performance today," said Charles Cheung, executive director at Shenzhen-based J&A Securities in Hong Kong.
"I expect the Hang Seng to move up to the 13,300 level resistance level and from there on, move in line with U.S. trends," said Cheung.
Cheung said that meant a continued advance toward Chinese New Year in early February with possibly minor pullbacks on the way.
On Wall Stree overnight, the Dow industrials added another 39 points to close above the 6,300 level for the first time at 6,313, and the S &P 500 hit a record of 736.
The November Hang Seng Index futures contract was trading 60 points higher at 13,014 after 40 minutes of trade.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market, followed by properties.
Trading hong Hutchison Whampoa added HK$1.00 to a new all time high of HK$60.50.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong led the most active list and also rose to a new high of HK$67.75 before easing to trade unchanged at HK$67.00 on turnover of HK$143.96 million.
Newcomer China Resources Beijing Land was the next most active, shedding HK$0.125 at HK$4.075 on robust turnover of HK$108.42 million.
